title: Noninvasive Ventilation for Preoxygenation during Emergency Intubation
shortTitle: PREOXI: a better start before intubation
summary: PREOXI randomized 1,301 critically ill adults to NIV or an oxygen mask before intubation. Hypoxemia (SpO2 <85%) occurred in 9.1% versus 18.5% (absolute difference -9.4 percentage points; 95% CI -13.2 to -5.6).
whyItMatters: Supports choosing NIV for preoxygenation in suitable critically ill adults to reduce peri-intubation hypoxemia. This studied regimen does not establish a survival benefit.
limitations: Unblinded trial in US EDs and ICUs. Applicability depends on patient suitability for NIV; infrequent safety events do not establish equivalence.
population: Critically ill adults undergoing intubation in 24 US EDs and ICUs.
primaryEndpoint: SpO2 <85% from induction through two minutes after intubation
findings: Hypoxemia: 57/624 (9.1%) with NIV vs 118/637 (18.5%) with an oxygen mask; difference -9.4 percentage points (95% CI -13.2 to -5.6).
Aspiration: 0.9% vs 1.4%; difference -0.4 percentage points (95% CI -1.6 to 0.7).
evidenceNotes: Abstract-based summary; methods text also checked for design. Open-access full text available for further appraisal.
